decisions.reason: As a technically adjacent but non-core sports system that has had several years to reveal demand, its remaining option value looks weaker than the benefit of refocusing on the firm's core interior flooring business.
A mobile arena floor is a specialized project product outside the firm's main style-led flooring focus, so management would likely abandon this peripheral option after limited traction.
Because it is another mobile arena-floor option in the same niche as B, the firm would likely prune this overlapping experiment and free resources for core lines and new development.
The chevron hardwood parquet fits the firm's stated flagship direction in trend-led, natural-looking interior floors, so it remains a strong core product to keep on the market.
A squash-court surface finish is a narrow niche with limited strategic fit to the firm's customer base, making it a likely candidate for exit once its value has largely been tested.
This sports-floor accessory depends on a peripheral product family rather than the firm's main collections, so it would likely be withdrawn if those sports options are not pursued further.
